doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Pop pressure, past producers and titling 'Home'
summary: Pop repertoire records with Matt Pierson and Jorge Calandrelli, return to the core, and choosing the title 'Home'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well do you have people telling you, “Oh listen, Jane, just go up in a more pop vein a little bit, try some of these pop tunes and it’ll pay off”?

Yeah I’ve been told that a lot, and luckily I really love pop tunes, you know making the record with Matt Pierson, “Lovers and Dreamers and Me” we did tons of pop repertoire and it was really fun, it was really fun, but I couldn’t really play it live. You know, making “Surrender” with Jorge Calandrelli we did sort of Brazilian stuff with a Brazilian pop feel, a lot of ballads and stuff like that, and it was really fun. That record we could play more live, because at the time I had a guitarist and a saxophone player in my band, it was a larger ensemble, but you know stuff like that, it’s been really fun doing these projects where we touch on this different repertoire. And for each thing I had the exact right producer for it, and it was cool. But it was time to get back to the core, and for that, it had to be me.
That sounds like a good title for your next record, “it had to be me.”
I didn’t think of that. You know we agonized over the title too.

Oh my God it took forever. It usually does, but this one was really like we need a title like today, Jane, what’s it going to be? And we ended up just calling it “Home” because that’s what it is. That’s what it is. It’s exactly that.
